neighbours.label: A verb or preposition whose object has been moved earlier in the sentence (a filler-gap site: 'what X and Y have _ in common', 'a list to explore _', 'a goal to aim for _', 'all you want to use _ is'); the same verbs with their object in place stay quiet.
fire: What do lions and house cats have in common?
She left me a stack of novels to read on the train.
Here is the address you asked for last week.
The only tool you need to bring is a hammer.
Which of these colours do you prefer for the kitchen?
That is the record I have been looking for all year.
He made a list of museums to visit in Paris.
Everything we discussed in the meeting is in the notes.
quiet: Lions and house cats have many traits in common.
She told me to read a stack of novels on the train.
Last week you asked for the address of the hotel.
You need to bring a hammer and some nails.
Do you prefer blue or green for the kitchen?
I have been looking for that record all year.
He planned to visit three museums in Paris.
We discussed the budget in the meeting this morning.
